previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for his ninth cycle of high-dose methotrexate since CNS lymphoma relapse, marking the fifth maintenance dose and second bimonthly administration. He tolerated the chemotherapy infusion well without complications. His candidal chest rash improved with topical miconazole, and he remained neurologically stable with no new deficits. Methotrexate levels were monitored and cleared appropriately. Liver enzymes rose transiently as expected. Aspirin and omeprazole were held during treatment and restarted at discharge. A brain MRI showed no new enhancing lesions, indicating stable disease. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up scheduled for the next cycle in two months.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  MR HEAD W AND W/O CONTRAST T___ MR HEAD

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with CNS lymphoma on methotrexate, HA and
vomiting  // restaging

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal and axial T1 weighted imaging were performed. After
administration of Gadavist intravenous contrast, axial imaging was performed
with gradient echo, FLAIR, diffusion, and T1 technique. Sagittal MPRAGE
imaging was performed and re-formatted in axial and coronal orientations.

COMPARISON:  MRI brain most recently from ___, dated back to ___.

FINDINGS: 

The previously seen lesion extending from the posterior limb of the left
internal capsule into the left cerebral peduncle of the midbrain demonstrates
stable high T2/FLAIR signal without evidence of residual contrast enhancement.
Multiple other smaller, foci of high FLAIR signal in the periventricular and
subcortical deep white matter are stable.  No new enhancing lesions are
identified.

No diffusion abnormalities concerning for infarction identified.  Linear
susceptibility artifacts seen in the posterior left frontal lobe at the vertex
is likely related to prior biopsy.  The ventricles are normal in size and
configuration.  There is no acute hemorrhage or shift of the midline
structures.

The arterial flow voids are well preserved.  There is diffuse mild mucosal
sinus thickening.  The left mastoid is not pneumatized as seen previously. 
Left parietal burr hole is re- demonstrated.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of acute intracranial abnormality.  No evidence of enhancing
mass lesion.  Stable T2/FLAIR hyperintense nonenhancing lesion extending from
the posterior limb of the left internal capsule into the left cerebral
peduncle of the midbrain.

2. Stable scattered nonspecific foci of T2/FLAIR signal abnormality in the
periventricular, subcortical skull, and deep white matter likely secondary to
small vessel ischemic disease.
